title: macOS tailscale logs out after less than 5 mins of signing in
body:
### What is the issue?

I click on sign in, it logs in successfully automatically.

Then after less than 5 minutes, tailscale logs itself out, vpn disconnects, saying "Please log in."

I repeat sign in again, it logs in successfully automatically. Repeat.

### Steps to reproduce

- open tailscale
- after it logs itself in, wait a couple of mins
- tailscale's VPN service stops running on its own (in system preferences, it got turned off)

### Are there any recent changes that introduced the issue?

I haven't ever experienced this issue, until I updated to`1.40.0`. I tried updating to `1.42.0` but it still has the same issue.

At the moment it signs itself out, the logs in macOS's Console show

```
Could not read metadata file at [/Users/<user>/Library/Group Containers/io.tailscale.ipn.macos.login-item-helper/.com.apple.containermanagerd.metadata.plist]; error = Error Domain=NSPOSIXErrorDomain Code=2 "No such file or directory" UserInfo={SourceFileLine=1835, NSLocalizedDescription=<~~~>, FunctionName=<~~~>}
```

### OS

macOS

### OS version

macOS Ventura 13.4

### Tailscale version

1.42.0

### Other software

LuLu

### Bug report

_No response_

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Ah, how awkward. After I posted this issue, the issue just stopped on its own. And I just found out how to generate logs by doing option + click, since there was no `tailscale` in the terminal, but it was already after the fact.

I'll reopen this issue if it happens again.

comments.author: participant23
comments.body: Hi folks, we can consistently reproduce this behavior in-house. We have tracked this down to CacheDelete, a framework in macOS. When macOS detects that disk space is running out, it attempts to clear the cache for every application on the system. Before doing so, CacheDelete terminates each process, to avoid pulling data from underneath a running app. However, terminating a VPN extension like ours means that the VPN will be forcibly disconnected. We're aware of reports that this affects other VPN apps as well, and we're currently investigating workarounds.
